purpose: A panel that slides in from an edge of the screen and keeps the page behind it in view. It holds secondary work that is too large or too long-lived for a dialog: filters, a long form, the details of a row, a navigation list. `Drawer.Content` is the whole modal: it teleports to `body`, renders the dimmed overlay, traps focus and scroll-locks the page, so the page behind cannot be clicked or tabbed to while it is open. The header gets the close (X) button on its own unless `closable` is false. It closes on Escape and on an overlay click when `dismissible`, and returns focus to its trigger. `:modal="false"` is the one opt-out: no overlay, no focus trap, no scroll lock, for a side panel that works next to the page it talks about (as Radix `modal={false}`).
useWhen: A panel that slides in from a screen edge for secondary tasks, filters, long forms, or navigation, while keeping page context.
The content is too large or persistent for a centered modal.
avoidWhen: It is a short, focused confirmation/task best centered and fully blocking → use `dialog`.
It is a small overlay anchored to a trigger → use a popover / `dropdown`.
related: dialog` — centered, blocking modal for focused tasks/confirmations.
bestPractices: Pick the edge (side) intentionally and keep it consistent across the app.
Do not add an overlay, a portal or a close button by hand: `Drawer.Content` renders the overlay and the portal, and the header renders the close button while `closable` is true (the default).
Keep the drawer modal (the default). Use `:modal="false"` only when the reader must keep reading or using the page beside the drawer, such as an assistant that answers questions about the page.
While an action is in flight, set `:dismissible="false"` and `:closable="false"` together so nothing can close it.

Bind the open state with `v-model:open`, or `:open` plus an `@update:open` handler typed `(open: boolean) => void`. The payload is always a `boolean`, so the handler needs no cast and no `Boolean(...)`.
